exposure: Race/ethnicity (American Indian/Alaska Native, Asian, non-Hispanic Black, non-Hispanic White, Hispanic, None of the above)
cohort: Pregnant individuals in the United States who provided data to the Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (PRAMS).
finding: Racial and ethnic disparities exist in influenza and Tdap vaccination rates among pregnant individuals in the United States, with Asian respondents showing the highest uptake and Black respondents the lowest; American Indian/Alaska Native uptake was higher for influenza but similar to White respondents for Tdap after adjustment.
cross-section timing: Data collected post-delivery reflecting vaccination status during pregnancy.
